opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin would require owning the system, which does not apply here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors without advanced training may have at most read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
reason: The two notes about E045 conflict on employment type: HR states full-time Engineer (max write), while Security states contractor with basic security training (max read for contractors without advanced training). Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist, not Engineer, so admin is not applicable in either case. Given the conflicting evidence, I grant the more conservative level, read, which complies with both interpretations and never exceeds the allowed maximum.
